title: Three Nights and One Short Thermometer
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：nose　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 nose 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the nurse ① held the nose that no sufferer in the ward would have measured, and he said the holding was the whole of the night. The ② nose, meaning the feature itself and not the thermometer, ran three nights and stayed unmeasured in the book; a nose, he said, is the only thing in a ward that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ nose in that ward had the same short thermometer beside it, and the ④ nose at the far cupboard, meaning the dose they kept for the children to take and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A nose, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the nurse said the measuring is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the nose was the whole of the matter, meaning the pride and not the feature. The ⑥ nose, meaning the pride and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; nose, he said, is either something you hold or the only word that means both a feature and a pride. He said the pride is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ nose had become a line in a report, and the report had become an argument about the short thermometer. The ⑧ nose of the whole thing, the nurse wrote in April, was one ward and three nights of measuring; nose, he said, is either the dose at the far cupboard or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ nose I remember is the feature measured in the report, which closed in 1966 and is still measured as the quietest in the ward. A ⑩ nose, my mother said in 1968, is the only feature that improves by being measured; every nose, she said, is a pride that has agreed to look like a feature. She said the pride was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 鼻子（指病房里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 鼻子（指那个鼻子本身，与细细的体温计相对）
C. 固定搭配：hold the nose 捏这一个鼻子
D. n. 鼻子（指留给孩子们服的那一剂）
E. n. 鼻子之事（抽象总称，指一处病房的鼻子之事）
F. n. 鼻子（指护理记录里写到、被测量的那一个）
G. n. 鼻子、自尊（指一件事里人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 自尊（抽象总称，指人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: held the nose that no sufferer in the ward would have measured
The nose, meaning the feature itself and not the thermometer
the nose at the far cupboard

answers.why: hold the nose 意为“捏这一个鼻子”，1959 年那位护士把病房里没有一位病患肯测量的一个鼻子做了一遍。
nose 意为“鼻子”，指那个鼻子本身而不是细细的体温计，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被测量。
nose 意为“鼻子”，指病房里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一支细细的体温计。
nose 意为“鼻子”，指最远那格药柜的留给孩子们服的那一剂，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
nose 意为“鼻子、自尊”，指一件事里人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个自尊就是那件事的全部。
nose 意为“自尊”，指人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个鼻子，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
nose 意为“鼻子”，指护理记录里写到、被测量的那一个，到 1964 年这一个成了护理记录里的一行。
nose 意为“鼻子之事”，护士四月写道，整件事的鼻子之事是一处病房和三个夜晚的测量。
nose 意为“鼻子”，我记得的是护理记录里测量过的那一个，1966 年挺过了，至今仍被说成病房里最安静的一个。
nose 为抽象总称，母亲 1968 年说，鼻子是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的鼻子。
